1: Tobit, a faithful Israelite deported to Nineveh, gives alms and buries the dead at risk to his life.
Faithfulness is possible in a hostile place.
2: After burying a man, Tobit sleeps outside and is blinded. He bears it patiently, though his wife reproaches him.
The just man is tested, like Job.
3: Tobit asks to die. Far away Sara, whose seven husbands were each killed by a demon, prays too. God hears both and sends the angel Raphael.
God answers two prayers with one plan.
4: Thinking he will die, Tobit instructs his son Tobias: honour your mother, give alms, and do to no one what you would hate. He tells him of money left in Media.
5: Tobias finds a companion for the journey, the angel Raphael in disguise.
God sends help we do not recognise at the time.
6: A great fish attacks Tobias at the river. Raphael tells him to keep its heart, liver and gall, and to marry Sara.
The remedy for both troubles is found on the way.
7: Sara's father Raguel welcomes them and gives her to Tobias in marriage.
Marriage is entered with family and blessing.
8: Tobias burns the fish's liver and the demon flees. The couple pray together before lying down.
Their prayer is read at Catholic weddings. Marriage is to be lived in prayer.
9: Raphael fetches the money and brings Gabelus to the wedding feast.
The original errand is done almost in passing.
10: Tobit and Anna fear their son is dead. Tobias takes leave of Sara's parents.
A blessing sends the young couple on their way.
11: Tobias returns, anoints his father's eyes with the fish's gall, and Tobit sees again.
Tobit blesses God for both chastising and healing him.
12: Offered wages, the guide says, "I am Raphael, one of the seven who stand before the Lord." He had carried their prayers to God.
Angels are real and present our prayers. Prayer with fasting and alms is good.
13: Tobit praises God, who scourges and saves, and foresees Jerusalem rebuilt in splendour.
14: Tobit dies in peace, telling his family to leave Nineveh. Tobias lives to see its fall.
A faithful life ends in peace.
